messages.content: Choose exactly one frozen method for this research benchmark partition BEFORE seeing any association labels, held-out metrics or other partition outcomes. Call submit_partition_choice once. Use only the supplied expression-feature summary and method definitions. If the summary is insufficient, still choose one method and state the uncertainty. Do not claim efficacy or unseen performance.

{"dataset": "TRANSCRIPT v2.0.0 disease partition", "disease_count": 29, "drug_count": 613, "expression_gene_count": 12096, "median_disease_signature_sd": 0.00825, "methods": {"B0p": "Training-fold positive association count per drug", "B1": "Label-free negative Spearman correlation between drug and disease expression", "B1k": "Training-fold label propagation from expression-similar drugs with 10 neighbors", "B2": "Fixed equal-weight reciprocal-rank fusion of B0p, B1k and B1 with k=60"}, "metric_to_optimize": "official NS-AUC", "partition_id": "transcript_disease_partition_02", "split": "random_simple", "split_description": "Hold out 20% of drug-disease pairs; the same drugs may occur in training"}

function.name: submit_partition_choice
function.arguments: {"method": "B2", "reason": "With 29 diseases, 613 drugs and ~12k expression genes, the split holds out 20% of drug-disease pairs while allowing the same drugs in training, so drug-level signals (B0p counts, label propagation through expression-similar drugs) and the disease-side expression correlation (B1) are all plausibly informative and complementary. B2 fuses these three into one fixed equal-weight reciprocal-rank score, which hedges against any single signal being weak or miscalibrated and requires no tuning that could overfit this small disease set. The provided summary confirms the components exist without revealing which is best, so the robust fusion is the safer prescore choice; uncertainty remains because the summary lacks per-method validation evidence, so actual NS-AUC performance is unverified."}
